summary: Donald R. Davis Jr. specializes in Indology and religious studies, having studied under Patrick Olivelle, Ludo Rocher, and Richard W. Lariviere. He was an associate professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2006–2012) and faculty at UT Austin (attested 2026).

Donald S. Lopez Jr. works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning a PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held positions at Middlebury College (1986) and the University of Michigan, where he was appointed Distinguished University Professor in 1990.
A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Dondub Buddhayin taught Eugène Obermiller. He served as abbot of Ganden Dargye Ling (attested 1933) and Chilttai Monastery.

id: P:Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso
summary: Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Dongak Chokyi Nyima studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Dongak Tendzin studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Dongchu worked in Buddhist studies, studying at Minnan Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He was dean at Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy (~1935–1945), abbot of Dinghui Monastery (~1944–1949), and served at Jing'an Temple Buddhist Academy (~1947–1949).
Donna C. Kurtz is an archaeologist and historian who earned her DPhil from Oxford. She held long-term posts at the University of Oxford and the Classical Art Research Centre (~1970–2011).

Donna Lynn Brown works in Buddhist and religious studies, earning an MA and PhD from the University of Manitoba, where she was a sessional instructor in 2023. She also served as an associate editor at FPMT (2016–2017).
Donna Strahan is an archaeology and history professional who served as conservator at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (attested 2010) and became Head at the National Museum of Asian Art in 2014.

Dor Bahadur Bista studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus and worked in Tibetology. He served as a professor at Tribhuvan University (~1975–1990) and was on the board of governors of the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development.
Doranne Jacobson works in Indology, earning a doctorate in anthropology from Columbia University, where she later served as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

Doris Meth Srinivasan studied under W. Norman Brown at the University of Pennsylvania (PhD). Specializing in art history, Indology, and religious studies, she held posts at Columbia, Barnard, George Washington University, and Stony Brook University (attested 2016, 2026).
Doris Unterthurner works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.
Dorje Rinchen (1819–1867) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Sakya Yab Jé Kün Ga Rinchen, Ja Shong Lob Zur Lodrö Gyatso, and others, and taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Dorje Tseten was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied education at Beijing Normal University (~1944–1948). He served as director of the China Tibetology Research Center from 1986 to 2000.

Dorji Banzarov (1822–1855) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at First Kazan Male Gymnasium and Kazan Imperial University (~1842–1846) under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski.

Dorji Penjore works in Tibetology and history, earning a PhD from Australian National University (2012–2016). He was Chief Researcher at the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH (2017–2021) and head/assistant professor at the Royal Institute of Management (2021–2026).

Dorji Wangchuk is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, becoming a professor there in 2009.

Dorothy C. Wong is a Buddhist studies and art history scholar who earned her PhD from Harvard University (1988–1995). She has held posts at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009) and the University of Virginia (attested 2026).
